speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the specific location of your right groin pain and tell me if you are able to bear weight on that leg? I also need to know if you heard or felt a "pop" or "snap" at the time of the accident.

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are you currently able to bear any weight on your right leg, and do you notice your right foot or leg resting in an externally rotated position compared to the left? Additionally, can you rate the severity of the groin pain on a scale of 1 to 10 and describe any numbness or tingling in the right leg?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_X-Ray

The presentation of a shortened, internally rotated, and adducted leg following high-energy trauma is classic for a posterior hip dislocation. I need to confirm the displacement and rule out associated fractures immediately.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic X-ray: No fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip.
